## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. Tech and crypto led the declines while the VIX, the dollar and yields rose.

## 2. What moved and why
**Tech sells off as inflation and rate-hike worries build**
Why it happened: Wholesale inflation rose on top of Tuesday's hot consumer inflation report, and Fed official Bowman said inflation pressures have lasted longer and are broadening.
Why it matters: Higher yields reduce the present value of long-dated tech earnings. Markets are also pricing the chance that the Fed raises rates again.

**Nvidia's CEO exit keeps AI stocks on edge**
Why it happened: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and the stock was down about 4% again today. The company reports earnings next week.
Why it matters: Nvidia is the AI trade's anchor, so uncertainty over its leadership spills into chip stocks and the Nasdaq.

**Bitcoin drops below $70,000 on stronger dollar and ETF outflows**
Why it happened: A stronger dollar and higher yields after the hot inflation data pressured bitcoin. Leveraged long positions were also forced to close and US spot ETFs saw outflows.
Why it matters: It is bitcoin's weakest level since August, and it shows crypto trading as a risk asset tied to rates.

## Deals
- **IPO: Anthropic → Nasdaq (ticker ANT)** (). 
- **Acquisition: PSP Investments → 50% of Enercare** (C$1.6 billion). A Canadian pension fund is taking a half-stake in an essential home-services platform.
- **Acquisition: AMD → Taalas** (). 

## 3. What's coming today
Nothing is scheduled today.

## 4. Canada corner

## 5. The takeaway
Hot inflation raises the odds of further Fed hikes, which pressures long-duration growth stocks, crypto and the dollar-sensitive parts of the market at the same time.

stories.title: Tech sells off as inflation and rate-hike worries build
stories.why_happened: Wholesale inflation rose on top of Tuesday's hot consumer inflation report, and Fed official Bowman said inflation pressures have lasted longer and are broadening.
stories.why_matters: Higher yields reduce the present value of long-dated tech earnings. Markets are also pricing the chance that the Fed raises rates again.
stories.full: Tuesday's October CPI came in hotter than expected. A key Fed official also hinted at a possible half-point rate rise next month. Treasury yields jumped on fears that more hikes could come in 2027. Friday's wholesale price data added to that. Bowman's comments pushed the same way, and the Nasdaq fell more than the S&P 500 as a result. The dollar index reached its highest level since April 2025. Higher-yielding assets and the dollar benefit from this setup. Growth stocks, crypto and rate-sensitive borrowers lose. Before today, investors had been rotating into under-owned parts of the market, which cushioned the index. Today that cushion looks thinner. Next up are October retail sales on Tuesday and the FOMC minutes on Wednesday. Both could shift expectations for December.

stories.full: Huang resigned after reports about his personal conduct. The shock has hit hard. Super Micro Computer fell 11% on Thursday. Rivals have gained: AMD and Broadcom rallied at the open today. Customers and rivals could gain if buyers decide to diversify their chip suppliers. Nvidia shareholders and its AI-linked suppliers bear the risk. Watch Nvidia's earnings next week. Investors will look for guidance on demand, plus any word on who runs the company.

intern.headline: Hot inflation and Nvidia turmoil hit tech stocks
intern.mood: Risk-off. Tech and crypto led the declines while the VIX (a gauge of how nervous stock investors are), the dollar and yields (the interest rate on bonds) rose.

stories.title: Tech sells off as inflation and rate-hike worries build
stories.why_happened: Wholesale inflation (the rise in prices that companies pay for goods) came in higher, on top of Tuesday's hot consumer inflation report. Fed official Bowman said inflation pressures have lasted longer and are spreading across the economy.
stories.why_matters: When yields rise, future tech profits look less valuable today. Investors are also betting the Fed (the US central bank) may raise interest rates again.
stories.full: Tuesday's October CPI (the main measure of consumer prices) came in hotter than expected. A key Fed official also hinted at a possible half-point rate rise next month. Treasury yields (the interest rate the US government pays on its loans) jumped on fears that more rate rises could come in 2027. Friday's wholesale price data added to those worries. Bowman's comments pushed in the same direction, and the Nasdaq (a stock index full of tech companies) fell more than the S&P 500 (a stock index of 500 large US companies). The dollar index (a score of the dollar's strength against other currencies) reached its highest level since April 2025. A strong dollar and higher yields help some investments. Growth stocks (companies expected to grow fast, often with profits far in the future), crypto and companies that borrow money at changing rates tend to lose. Before today, investors had been moving money into parts of the market that had been ignored, which cushioned the index. Today that cushion looks thinner. Next up are October retail sales on Tuesday and the FOMC minutes (notes from the Fed's policy meeting) on Wednesday. Both could change expectations for December.

stories.title: Nvidia's CEO exit keeps AI stocks on edge
stories.why_happened: Nvidia CEO (chief executive, the top boss) Jensen Huang resigned, and the stock was down about 4% again today. The company reports earnings (its profit results) next week.
stories.why_matters: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade (investing in companies that build artificial intelligence). Doubt about its leadership spreads to chip stocks and the Nasdaq.
stories.full: Huang resigned after reports about his personal conduct. The shock has hit hard. The stock was down 11% on the week as of Thursday. It is more than 30% below its October 6 peak. That wiped out about $1.8 trillion of market value in five weeks. The damage has spread. Super Micro Computer fell 11% on Thursday. Rivals have gained. AMD and Broadcom rallied at the open today. Customers and rivals could gain if buyers decide to spread their chip orders across more suppliers. Nvidia shareholders (people who own its stock) and its AI-linked suppliers carry the risk. Watch Nvidia's earnings next week. Investors will look for guidance (the company's outlook for future sales) on demand, plus any news about who will run the company.

stories.title: Bitcoin drops below $70,000 on stronger dollar and ETF outflows
stories.why_happened: A stronger dollar and higher yields after the hot inflation data pressured bitcoin (a digital currency). Leveraged long positions (bets that prices will rise, made with borrowed money) were also forced to close. US spot ETFs (funds that hold bitcoin directly and trade like stocks) saw outflows, meaning investors took money out.
stories.why_matters: This is bitcoin's weakest level since August. It shows that crypto moves with interest rates and the dollar, not apart from them.
stories.full: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August. It hit a low near $67,600. It is on pace for a sixth straight weekly decline. The sell-off fed on itself. About $1.47 billion of leveraged positions were liquidated (forced to close), mostly bets that prices would rise. US spot ETFs lost about $1.44 billion over five sessions through November 11. The Fear & Greed index (a score of how scared or excited investors are) fell to 20, which is extreme fear. Leveraged traders and ETF holders lost the most. Bitcoin is now about 45% below its October 2025 peak. Traders are watching $65,000 as a possible next floor to fall to. $70,000 is now resistance (a price level where selling tends to show up). Further strength in the dollar would add pressure.

deals.type: IPO (Initial Public Offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public)
deals.why: It is one of the largest IPOs ever.
deals.full: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at $70–$78 each. That implies roughly $58–64 billion raised. It is seeking a valuation (the total price of the whole company) near $1.4 trillion. The offering is one of the largest IPOs ever.

deals.why: A Canadian pension fund is taking a half-stake in an essential home-services platform.

A Canadian pension fund (a fund that invests money to pay future retirement benefits) is taking a half-stake in an essential home-services platform (a business that delivers home services, such as heating and cooling).

intern.takeaway: When inflation runs hot, interest rates and bond yields tend to rise, and that pulls down prices of risky, fast-growing assets like tech stocks and bitcoin.
intern.takeaway_accounting: Higher yields lower the present value of future cash flows, so long-dated earnings are worth less today.
intern.takeaway_consulting: Today's selloff shows how one company's leadership shock, like Nvidia's CEO exit, can spread across an entire sector and its suppliers.
